cells.tense: A direction has caught you and you're moving by it while it still costs you little.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Keep going toward what you want through one more stretch of doubt, without checking whether it's still right. No permission, no gut-check. Stay on it and see what the week is like when you don't ask for proof.
cells.core:
There's something you couldn't name a while back, and now you can — and you're still on it. Getting started is the easy part for you here; it's the staying that's about to be tested. The direction you chose is real, it's holding, and you're not asking it to prove itself yet.

The next move keeps what's working, and if you forget, the pull doesn't quit. Keep steering by the want you've already recognised through one more stretch of doubt. You don't need a reason to go on, or a sign it's still right. Going is the reason. If a week passes and you've kept at it without checking the sky, you've done the thing this part of you is for.
cells.sheetLine: You're on it, and not asking it to prove itself.
cells.verb: lighting something before there's a name for it
cells.place: the place where the pull toward what's wanted is felt

cells.tense: The thing you love hasn't happened yet and you're already bracing for how you'll fail at it.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Spread what you're imagining onto a page or a table — what done looks like, what it would take, what could stop it — so nothing about it stays hidden from you. Look it over, then close the notebook. Don't start anything yet.
cells.core:
You've got a want and it's going well, except it hasn't happened yet and the picture of it keeps getting ahead of you. You're not just holding something bright — you're editing the ending before the thing has a chance to start, preparing a story about how it'll go wrong, whether you'll get there, whether you deserve to. That's the bright thing already under audit, not plain sight.

There's a difference between the light you'll actually have and the proof of the light you're chasing. Pull all of it out of your head and onto one page, whole, done or not. When every piece is in view at once, the bracing stops for a minute. What you want stays, and you don't have to perform it. Go back to the open beginning for a few days and see what the thing is like before you've decided.
cells.sheetLine: What you want is real. You're bracing before it arrives.

cells.place: the place where the pull toward what's wanted is felt

cells.tense: The door is behind you now, and you're still standing where it used to be.
cells.act: take in the whole rainbow of what you feel
cells.ask: Gather every feeling you have about what you wanted — the ache, the relief, the fear of wanting it — each one its own word on a page. Leave all of it there, nothing crossed out, and don't decide anything after.
cells.core:
Something you wanted was at a door, and the door is behind you now; the pull is here but the beginning isn't. The want has been waiting so long it's started reading like a fantasy rather than a direction, and the distance between what you want and where you're standing has stopped being fuel and started being a subject you avoid.

Before the light comes back, the feeling about it needs to be whole. Take in the full rainbow of what you actually feel about this want — the ache of it, the relief of it, the fear of being seen wanting it. Get every colour onto one sheet, none of it crossed out. Nobody's asking you to take a step toward it yet. Just stop leaving part of it off the page, and see the whole of where you actually stand.
cells.sheetLine: What you want is real. The door behind you is real too.
cells.verb: lighting something before there's a name for it
cells.place: the place where the pull toward what's wanted is felt

cells.tense: Something is catching fire in you and you're calling it just the way things go.
cells.act: use the finished thing for an hour instead of improving it
cells.ask: Stop reaching past what you've already imagined and finished anything on. Spend an hour inside it as it is — no edits, no next step. Then notice what you made is yours.
cells.core:
There's a spark of want in you, and you already have the direction — you can point to where the fire started. You'd describe it as just wanting a change, or being bored. The thing you wanted is already partway here, and the person who wanted it is you. The pull to light is operating; you just haven't put your name on what you're after.

Use what you already made once, exactly as it is, for an hour. Don't improve it, just use it, and notice it's yours. The dream runs on a finished feeling, and you've been skipping the part where you stand in it. An hour inside what you wanted, no edits, is how the pull becomes yours instead of something that just happens to you. Then it's yours to steer, or yours to let go.
cells.sheetLine: The fire's yours. You've been calling it just the way things go.

attempts.check: The record supports the drawing itself, but says nothing about what already started, how long it's been going, who else is involved, or what kind of ending is wanted — so the cells name only the spark and what this part of a life currently does with it. A reader could reasonably say 'nothing is beginning for me right now' — the Too Little cell is built so that if the door is still shut, the act of sorting what you already wanted still teaches something. The ask survives a wrong read at every status. The line serving me more than them would be a clean arc: 'you are on your way to something shining.' There is no arc in the record; there is a seed and a pull. I fixed that by leaving the outcome unnamed everywhere.
